integrity_amendment: First attempt failed before writing a result because a replay assertion passed a decimal numerator string to Fraction(numerator, denominator), which requires an integer. Convert only the three result-row numerator strings to int inside replay assertions and re-pin the runner. The frozen model, matrix, result path, hypotheses and budgets are unchanged; no output from the failed attempt is accepted.
question: How much of the frozen IID prior is in distinct first-flux sectors reached by zero, one or two physical red-X edges, and can simple flux-weight/prior equivalence or direct law cost make these sectors tractable?

hypotheses.few_prior_classes: All single-edge sectors and the pair sectors within a common flux-weight class have the same exact sector prior, making a later symmetry proof worth testing without assuming law equivalence.
hypotheses.many_prior_classes: Pair sectors vary in exact prior within a common flux-weight class, rejecting a naive boundary-weight symmetry shortcut.
hypotheses.direct_cost_censored: Even one direct first law for each compatible private error in all reached sectors requires more than 65,536 projector terms, motivating a separate validated reduction rather than exhaustive Born evaluation.

frozen_model: R6AF ideal periodic L=2 D4 geometry and 36 IID red-X physical edges at p_X=1/10, p_Z=0. First public flux is the 24-bit pre-action J6O boundary. J8O's two specified complete first records, signal-only first-observation timing, relation-free fixed public actions, action-conditioned second-record convention, and private generation/scoring boundary remain unchanged; this is a prior-only screen with zero first/second public-law evaluation.

branches: Enumerate every zero-, one- and two-edge physical support; deduplicate its public first-flux sector and sum each sector's exact IID prior over all 8,192 compatible errors. Report reached-sector and complementary prior mass with exact rational arithmetic.

Group reached sectors by minimum observed support weight, flux Hamming weight and exact sector prior. Test single-edge prior equality and whether each pair-flux-weight class splits into multiple prior values. Project the absolute lower bound of one direct first-law term per compatible private error; do not evaluate those Born laws.
matrix.independent_unit: One distinct public first-flux GF(2) coset; 8,192 compatible private red-X errors are summed by integer weights for that coset. No random sampling or uncertainty interval.
matrix.integrity: Pin inputs and runner; verify rank 23/nullity 13, 8,192 distinct kernel elements, 1+36+630 low-weight supports, exact IID normalization, J8O vacuum and one-edge sector-prior replay, distinct first-flux deduplication, reached/unreached prior partition, no new Born terms, and hashes before/after. Matching sector priors are only arithmetic equivalence, never an asserted geometry or public-law symmetry.

acceptance: Exact count and IID prior mass of all first-flux sectors reached by <=2 red-X edges and the complementary mass
Exact prior-equivalence class count by minimum support and flux weight, with explicit non-symmetry claim boundary
Direct per-error first-law term lower-bound versus inherited 65,536-term ceiling, without evaluating any first or second law
stop_rule: Stop at all <=2-edge supports, first integrity failure, 5,464,064 integer-weight evaluations or 60 CPU seconds. Do not add weight-3 sectors, evaluate Born laws, infer operator-law symmetry, full-IID information/risk, noisy JIT or threshold.
